title.narrative: African Geological Surveys and the Organisation of African Geological Surveys are more effective in terms of national, regional and continental support to policy making and planning processes

description.narrative: During the first period (22 June 202130 June 2022), different points are related to the outcome of the Action:PanAfGeo was invited at the African Union Expert Group Meetings hold in Nairobi, Kenya from 01 to 05 November 2021. The expert group meeting was centred on the following objectives: (1) Developing guidelines on the ASM Strategy; (2) Reviewing the progress of the development of Model Minerals Laws, and (3) Progressing towards the implementation of the African Minerals Geoscience Initiative AMGI. Mr. JeanClaude Guillaneau (Coordination) participated in the different expert group meetings and also made a presentation about the Action.During the Mining Indaba Conference hold in Cape Town, South Africa (0912 May 2022), a special PanAfGeo session entitled A stronger AfricaEU geoscientific cooperation programme was organised on 9th May 2022. During this meeting, Frank Mugyenyi (Minerals Africa Development Institution, MADI) accentuated the importance of mineral resources in the context of AfricaEU cooperation, noting in particular the African Unions recently established African Mineral and Energy Resources Classification and Management System (AMREC). Mr. Mugyenyi welcomed the fact that PanAfGeo has generated a greater interest in the sector. Moreover, Ms. Rasa JautakaiteTunaitiene (Delegation of the European Union to South Africa) emphasized development and cooperation activities between the two continents by using the example of the PanAfGeo Project, and how it paves the way for future AfricaEU cooperation in line with highlevel policy dialogues on the green transition.From 03 to 09 April 2022, a training session dealing with geohazards and environmental management of mines has been carried out in Douala, Cameroon (WPE). This session provides the necessary knowledge for African Geological Surveys staff to be more effective at the national level in natural hazard management, landuse planning and measures to control potential pollution from mining activities. At least three more WPE training sessions will be organised during the second and third periods of the action, contributing to this outcome.From 13 to 18 June 2022, a training session dealing with geoheritage was organised in PointeNoire, Congo (WPD). This training session, led by the Polish Geological Survey (PGI) with the strong support of the French Geological Survey (BRGM) and the Spanish Geological (IGMECSIC), was organised in close cooperation with the Geological Survey of Congo and UNESCO. The training was strongly supported by the State Minister and Minister of Mines of Congo, H.E. Pierre Oba. This PanAfGeo training session (WPD) gave the opportunity to the Minister to attend the training and get useful information for supporting national policy making and planning processes. Indeed, H.E. Pierre Oba aims to develop geoconservation in Congo through the implementation of a geoheritage national inventory and then the proposal of a national geological interest park. Then, Congo would like to present an application for UNESCO Global Geopark label. Two more WPD training sessions dealing with geoheritage will be organised during the second period, contributing to the outcome.

title.narrative: Number of supported CSOs having established working partnerships with public authorities

description.narrative: Civil society is highly heterogeneous and encompasses a wide range of actors and aims. The EU considers civil society organisations to embrace a wide range of actors with multiple roles and mandates which includes all nonState, notforprofit, independent and nonviolent structures, through which people organise to pursue shared objectives and ideals, whether political, cultural, religious, environmental, social or economic or related to health. They include, but are not limited to: Nongovernmental organisations, organisations representing indigenous peoples, womens and youth organisations, diaspora organisations, migrants organisations, local traders associations and citizens groups, cooperatives, employers associations and trade unions (social partners), organisations representing economic and social interests, organisations fighting corruption and fraud and promoting good governance, civil rights organisations and organisations combating discrimination, local organisations (including networks) involved in decentralised regional cooperation and integration, consumer organisations, environmental, teaching, cultural, research and scientific organisations, universities, churches and religious associations and communities, philosophical and nonconfessional organisations, the notforprofit media and any nongovernmental associations and independent foundations, including independent political foundations.This large number of fields of activity of civil society means their initiatives can feature in a wide variety of EU interventions. See for more background: https://tacso.eu/dgnearguidelinesforeusupporttocivilsocietyintheenlargementregion20212027/Strictly speaking, the indicator does not require a CSO to have established working partnerships with public authorities through the intervention. It may have strengthened its capacity by means of the action and built the partnerships by itself afterwards or during the action but without direct support in that concrete activity. Public authority will be interpreted in accordance with the Inspire definition (https://inspire.ec.europa.eu/): any government or other public administration, including public advisory bodies, at national, regional or local level, and any natural or legal person performing public administrative functions under national law, including specific duties. This includes e.g. individual ministries and agencies but also municipal utility companies.A working partnership means actual collaboration where two sides (CSO and public authority) work together to improve something, e.g. the quality of policies or legislation in a certain field. Established means that both sides (CSO and public authority) have confirmed the partnership, e.g. by means of an MoU, (or equivalent written document) and that there is a concrete plan or intention to undertake specific, joint activities.

title.narrative: African Geological Surveys and the Organisation of African Geological Surveys are more effective in terms of national, regional and continental support to policy making and planning processes

description.narrative: During the first period (22 June 202130 June 2022), different points are related to the outcome of the Action:PanAfGeo was invited at the African Union Expert Group Meetings hold in Nairobi, Kenya from 01 to 05 November 2021. The expert group meeting was centred on the following objectives: (1) Developing guidelines on the ASM Strategy; (2) Reviewing the progress of the development of Model Minerals Laws, and (3) Progressing towards the implementation of the African Minerals Geoscience Initiative AMGI. Mr. JeanClaude Guillaneau (Coordination) participated in the different expert group meetings and also made a presentation about the Action.During the Mining Indaba Conference hold in Cape Town, South Africa (0912 May 2022), a special PanAfGeo session entitled A stronger AfricaEU geoscientific cooperation programme was organised on 9th May 2022. During this meeting, Frank Mugyenyi (Minerals Africa Development Institution, MADI) accentuated the importance of mineral resources in the context of AfricaEU cooperation, noting in particular the African Unions recently established African Mineral and Energy Resources Classification and Management System (AMREC). Mr. Mugyenyi welcomed the fact that PanAfGeo has generated a greater interest in the sector. Moreover, Ms. Rasa JautakaiteTunaitiene (Delegation of the European Union to South Africa) emphasized development and cooperation activities between the two continents by using the example of the PanAfGeo Project, and how it paves the way for future AfricaEU cooperation in line with highlevel policy dialogues on the green transition.From 03 to 09 April 2022, a training session dealing with geohazards and environmental management of mines has been carried out in Douala, Cameroon (WPE). This session provides the necessary knowledge for African Geological Surveys staff to be more effective at the national level in natural hazard management, landuse planning and measures to control potential pollution from mining activities. At least three more WPE training sessions will be organised during the second and third periods of the action, contributing to this outcome.From 13 to 18 June 2022, a training session dealing with geoheritage was organised in PointeNoire, Congo (WPD). This training session, led by the Polish Geological Survey (PGI) with the strong support of the French Geological Survey (BRGM) and the Spanish Geological (IGMECSIC), was organised in close cooperation with the Geological Survey of Congo and UNESCO. The training was strongly supported by the State Minister and Minister of Mines of Congo, H.E. Pierre Oba. This PanAfGeo training session (WPD) gave the opportunity to the Minister to attend the training and get useful information for supporting national policy making and planning processes. Indeed, H.E. Pierre Oba aims to develop geoconservation in Congo through the implementation of a geoheritage national inventory and then the proposal of a national geological interest park. Then, Congo would like to present an application for UNESCO Global Geopark label. Two more WPD training sessions dealing with geoheritage will be organised during the second period, contributing to the outcome.

description.narrative: For the first period, the Output 2 is starting and progressing thanks to the Frenchspeaking training session of WPE Geohazards & Environmental Management of Mines and the Frenchspeaking one of WPD Geoheritage organised in Cameroon (0309 April 2022), and in Congo (1318 June 2022), respectively. Total of 50 trainees (19 women and 31 men) coming from 15 African Geological Surveys benefited from increase skills in geoscientific and technological knowledge. Following the WPD Geoheritage training session, Congo would like to present an application for UNESCO Global Geopark label. Algeria, Niger, and Senegal also expressed their great interest to continue their geoheritage national inventory. Other participants acknowledge PanAfGeo for all geoscientific knowledge and skills brought during this training session, and are motivated to promote and develop geoheritage in their countries (e.g. by initiating inventories). It should be noted that a colleague from Niger who participated in the WPD training session became a trainer as he gave a training session on geoheritage to his colleagues from the Geological Survey of Niger.

description.narrative: The Output 1 is starting. Only two training sessions have been carried out during the first period and it is too early to have clear results for the Output 1. Nevertheless, the Phase2 is in the continuity with the Phase1 of the Action (20162020). During the period between the two phases, results can be exposed here partially resulting from the Phase1 of the Action. In Malawi, a major project of geological mapping and mineral resources assessment (GEMMAP) just published main results. A total of 53 geological maps (1:1,000,000, 1:250,000 and 1:100,000scales) has been published accompanied by 10 geohazards maps (1:200,000scale), 53 explanatory notes and important reports dealing with geohazards, mineral resources assessment and artisanal and smallscale mining. Some Malawian staff from the Geological Survey Department who have been involved in GEMMAP have been trained in the framework of PanAfGeo1 to different skills: geoscientific mapping (6 persons), geohazards (2 persons), mineral resources assessment (2 persons), artisanal and smallscale mining (32 persons, also outside Geological Survey). The Action clearly shows its contribution to other national projects in African countries. The case is similar in Cameroon, where another big geological mapping project (PRECASEM) just ended with the delivery of 35 geological maps (1:1,000,000 and 1:200,000scales). In Cameroon, 14 people have been trained to geological mapping and 13 to minerals resources assessment during the Phase1 of the Action. Still in Cameroon, alongside this geological mapping project, the elaboration of a Spatial Data Infrastructure (SDI) was carried out. Once again, some colleagues (8 persons) from the Cameroonian Ministry of Mines and Geology who was involved in the elaboration of this SDI, have been trained in the framework of PanAfGeo1 to geoscientific information management.This Output 1 will be continually reinforced during the second and the third periods of the Action with the organisation of more training sessions related to all WPs.

description.narrative: The Output 3 is starting and progressing. On June 2022, Dr. Rokhaya Samba Diene (OAGS President) informed the Action team that the National Geological Survey of Senegal (Service Gologique National du Sngal, SGNS) was officially created. Dr. Rokhaya Samba Diene is appointed General Director of SGNS. Citation of the Minister of Mines and Geology of Senegal, H.E. Oumar Sarr: In my opinion, SGNS will allow a better knowledge of our geological heritage, through an efficient system of acquisition, processing, interpretation and dissemination of geoscientific data. This department also plans to contribute through the rationalisation of financial resources in an efficient and transparent manner, and the optimisation and equitable sharing of the benefits of mining. In doing so, he intends to make the mining and geological sector an important contribution to the Senegalese economy through the emergency programme for the employment and integration of young people. Moreover, Dr. Samba Diene mentioned, during the Kickoff meeting (2526 November 2022), the entire satisfaction of OAGS through the Phase1 which brought an immeasurable contribution to the African geological surveys and the first political achievement for the AU and EU partnership. The creation of the National Geological Survey of Senegal relies on skilled staff in geosciences who have beneficiated of training sessions of PanAfGeo. During Phase1, 27 Senegalese colleagues have been trained.The organisation of the PanAfGeo special session A stronger AfricaEU geoscientific cooperation programme (09 May 2022) as a sideevent to Mining Indaba 2022, was the occasion to facilitate exchanges between EGS, OAGS and their respective members.The Minerals Africa Development Institution (MADI) on behalf of the African Union invited PanAfGeo to present the Action during the African Union Expert Group Meetings (Nairobi, Kenya, 0105 November 2021), and to participate to the working groups.Following the WPD Geoheritage training session (1318 June 2022) organised in close cooperation with UNESCO, the international institution as PanAfGeo stakeholder expressed its interest in exchanges with the African and European Geological Surveys, especially concerning the Global Geopark label and the International Geoscience Programme (IGCP). IGCP serves as a knowledge hub of UNESCO to facilitate international scientific cooperation in the geosciences. In that way, UNESCO invites PanAfGeo to participate to an international workshop promoting Global Geopark concept to Eastern/Southern Englishspeaking African countries. This workshop will be organised in Kenya from 05 to 12 November 2022, where will attend UNESCO National commissions and government representatives.Moreover, in the framework of the Colloquium of African Geology (CAG28), the Geological Society of Africa (GSAf) invites PanAfGeo to present as a keyspeaker the Action on July 2022 (second period).

title.narrative: Governance and dissemination tools for natural resources related policy sectors are operational

description.narrative: The Output 3 is starting and progressing. On June 2022, Dr. Rokhaya Samba Diene (OAGS President) informed the Action team that the National Geological Survey of Senegal (Service Gologique National du Sngal, SGNS) was officially created. Dr. Rokhaya Samba Diene is appointed General Director of SGNS. Citation of the Minister of Mines and Geology of Senegal, H.E. Oumar Sarr: In my opinion, SGNS will allow a better knowledge of our geological heritage, through an efficient system of acquisition, processing, interpretation and dissemination of geoscientific data. This department also plans to contribute through the rationalisation of financial resources in an efficient and transparent manner, and the optimisation and equitable sharing of the benefits of mining. In doing so, he intends to make the mining and geological sector an important contribution to the Senegalese economy through the emergency programme for the employment and integration of young people. Moreover, Dr. Samba Diene mentioned, during the Kickoff meeting (2526 November 2022), the entire satisfaction of OAGS through the Phase1 which brought an immeasurable contribution to the African geological surveys and the first political achievement for the AU and EU partnership. The creation of the National Geological Survey of Senegal relies on skilled staff in geosciences who have beneficiated of training sessions of PanAfGeo. During Phase1, 27 Senegalese colleagues have been trained.The organisation of the PanAfGeo special session A stronger AfricaEU geoscientific cooperation programme (09 May 2022) as a sideevent to Mining Indaba 2022, was the occasion to facilitate exchanges between EGS, OAGS and their respective members.The Minerals Africa Development Institution (MADI) on behalf of the African Union invited PanAfGeo to present the Action during the African Union Expert Group Meetings (Nairobi, Kenya, 0105 November 2021), and to participate to the working groups.Following the WPD Geoheritage training session (1318 June 2022) organised in close cooperation with UNESCO, the international institution as PanAfGeo stakeholder expressed its interest in exchanges with the African and European Geological Surveys, especially concerning the Global Geopark label and the International Geoscience Programme (IGCP). IGCP serves as a knowledge hub of UNESCO to facilitate international scientific cooperation in the geosciences. In that way, UNESCO invites PanAfGeo to participate to an international workshop promoting Global Geopark concept to Eastern/Southern Englishspeaking African countries. This workshop will be organised in Kenya from 05 to 12 November 2022, where will attend UNESCO National commissions and government representatives.Moreover, in the framework of the Colloquium of African Geology (CAG28), the Geological Society of Africa (GSAf) invites PanAfGeo to present as a keyspeaker the Action on July 2022 (second period).
